Twin
TWIN
noun (Gen-Z slang)
From English twin, one of two born at a birth. Twinning — two friends dressing or acting alike, usually in a matching photo — spread on social media in the 2010s. In the early 2020s twin became a term of address for a close friend ("what’s good, twin"), rising out of hip-hop and Black American speech and then through TikTok c. 2022–2023, where it is also used approvingly of anyone who shares your taste or opinion ("twin, we’re the same").

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

In current slang twin is a close friend, the one so like you that you might have shared a womb: "that’s my twin," or as an address, "you good, twin?" Twinning is dressing alike or thinking alike. It is a warm word, and much of the time it is simple affection. The Christian observation: Scripture’s most famous twins were not friends. "Behold, there were twins in her womb" (Gen 25:24), and Jacob and Esau struggled before they were born and for decades after; sameness of birth did not make sameness of heart. Real friendship in the Bible is a knitting of souls — "the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul" (1Sa 18:1) — and two very different men can be knit closer than twins. The slang tends to prize the friend who mirrors me; Scripture prizes the friend who sharpens me: "Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend" (Pro 27:17). And choose your twin with care, because you will become like him: "He that walketh with wise men shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed" (Pro 13:20). The deepest likeness is not to a friend at all. God has predestinated His people "to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren" (Rom 8:29). A father tells his daughter: find friends who look like Christ more than they look like you, and you will grow alike in the best way.

Webster 1828 Definition

Gen-Z slang (social-media twinning 2010s; address for a close friend c. 2022–present) for a best friend or kindred spirit — a warm word Scripture deepens from the friend who mirrors me to the friend who sharpens me toward the image of Christ.

expand to see more

TWIN, n. (Gen-Z slang, c. 2022–present; hip-hop and TikTok) A close friend; one who shares your taste, look, or opinion; also a term of address. "Twin, you have to come Saturday."

Twinning, v. and n., dressing or acting alike, often in matching photos. "Twin behaviour" — doing exactly what your friend would do.

The ordinary sense a grandparent knows: one of two children born at one birth, as Jacob and Esau (Gen 25:24).

Webster (1828), root word twin: “TWIN, noun 1. One of two young produced at a birth by an animal that ordinarily brings but one; used mostly in the plural, twins; applied to the young of beasts, as well as to human beings. 2. A sign of the zodiac; Gemini. 3. One very much resembling another.”

Decode for parents: an affectionate term for a best friend; ask who your child’s twin is and what that friend is making them like.

Key Scripture

Gen 25:24 — "And when her days to be delivered were fulfilled, behold, there were twins in her womb."

1Sa 18:1 — "And it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking unto Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul."

Pro 27:17 — "Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend."

Pro 13:20 — "He that walketh with wise men shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed."

Rom 8:29 — "For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren."

Modern Corruption

Twin is a warm word for a friend, which slides easily into prizing the friend who mirrors me over the friend who sharpens me toward Christ.

expand to see more

The word has real beauty in it. A friend so close you could have shared a birthday is a gift from God, and David found one in Jonathan, whose soul "was knit with the soul of David" (1Sa 18:1). There is nothing wrong with two girls showing up in matching sweaters or two boys finishing each other’s jokes. Scripture celebrates "a friend that sticketh closer than a brother" (Pro 18:24), and the slang is closest to grace when it means that.

The drift is toward sameness for its own sake. A friend chosen because he agrees with everything I already think cannot sharpen me; iron does not sharpen iron by matching it, but by striking it (Pro 27:17). The Bible’s actual twins are a warning that likeness of birth is not likeness of heart (Gen 25:24), and its promise points elsewhere: the Father is making a family who all resemble one Brother, Christ, "the firstborn among many brethren" (Rom 8:29). Teach your children to want that likeness above every other, and to pick friends who help them toward it.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English twinn (twofold, double) → twin, one of two born together → 2010s twinning (matching) → c. 2022 twin as address for a best friend.

Old English twinn — double, twofold; kin to two and twain

English twin — one of two born at a birth (Gen 25:24)

2010s social media: twinning, matching outfits and poses

c. 2022–2023 hip-hop and TikTok: twin as a term of address for a close friend

Usage

""Twin, you literally said what I was thinking.""

"Iron sharpeneth iron (Pro 27:17) — a good twin sharpens you, not just mirrors you."

"The best likeness is to Christ, the firstborn among many brethren (Rom 8:29)."
